_client_rules: Decisions confirmed by the client, applied by the pipeline rather than by hand:
A. A blank workbook cell means NO CHANGE. It never clears a tracker value.

stays an administrator's job in the app, so tracker_only_decisions is empty
by policy and not merely because nothing was decided.

re-derived from the three CAPP columns.

_renames: Tenaya Cottages has been funded and has moved from the development pipeline
onto the PARKS capital sheet as 'Cottages FFE Renovation' with CAPP 08745.
It matched nothing automatically because it gained an identifier and a name
in the same cycle, which is exactly the case this block exists for.
The evidence it is one project and not two:
- Same business unit, Parks & Resorts.
- Bill Nielsen on both: development lead on tracker 78, project manager on
the workbook row.
- Tracker 78's scope is 'Full FFE Remodel'; the row is 'Cottages FFE
Renovation' at TENAYA, and 78 is named 'Tenaya Cottages'.
- The narrative runs straight on. 78 reads 'Re-engaging with the designers
to do model room' (0925), then 'Received proposal from designer to provide
specs and drawings. Negotiating price.' (1009). The row now reads
'Awaiting CAPP for design to be approved so we can release A+P to move
forward with specs and drawings.'
- 78 disappeared from the development sheet in the same workbook in which
this PARKS row appeared.
- Every cost on the row is 0 and every date is TBD, which is what an
unapproved CAPP looks like.
Merging keeps the project's id and both existing history entries. Creating a
new project would strand them on a pipeline row no workbook mentions again.
relocate carries the four columns that place a project rather than describe
it. venue and section_name follow the sheet, which labels the block 'TENAYA'
the way every other PARKS block labels its own.
